es: Repasar cómo el tono, el registro y lo implícito cambian el significado de un mensaje y clasificar mensajes breves.

teaching.en: Her warm tone made the bad news easier to hear.
teaching.es: Su tono cordial hizo más fácil oír la mala noticia.
teaching.explanationEs: El tono es la actitud del mensaje: cordial (warm), seco, enfadado o sarcástico.
teaching.audioText: Her warm tone made the bad news easier to hear.

teaching.en: “Wow, what lovely weather,” he said in a sarcastic voice, while it rained.
teaching.es: «Vaya, qué buen tiempo», dijo con voz sarcástica mientras llovía.
teaching.explanationEs: Sarcasmo: las palabras son positivas, pero el sentido es el contrario. Lo delata el contexto.
segments: “Wow, what lovely weather,” he said in
a sarcastic voice, while it rained.
teaching.audioText: “Wow, what lovely weather,” he said in a sarcastic voice, while it rained.

teaching.en: I would be grateful if you could confirm the date.
teaching.es: Le agradecería que pudiera confirmar la fecha.
teaching.explanationEs: Registro formal: would be grateful if you could + verbo base, sin contracciones.
teaching.audioText: I would be grateful if you could confirm the date.

teaching.en: His blunt reply, “No,” ended the chat.
teaching.es: Su respuesta brusca, «No», puso fin a la conversación.
teaching.explanationEs: Blunt: dice la idea sin suavizarla. Sin please ni motivo, suena seco.
teaching.audioText: His blunt reply, “No,” ended the chat.

teaching.en: She dropped a hint: “It's a bit cold in here.”
teaching.es: Dejó caer una indirecta: «Hace un poco de frío aquí.»
teaching.explanationEs: Indirecta: la frase describe un hecho, pero pide una acción (cerrar la ventana). Lo implícito se deduce.
teaching.audioText: She dropped a hint: “It's a bit cold in here.”

teaching.en: We use a different register with friends and with a manager.
teaching.es: Usamos un registro distinto con amigos y con un jefe.
teaching.explanationEs: Registro: nivel de formalidad. Hey, can you…? con amigos; I was wondering if… con un jefe.
segments: We use a different register with
teaching.audioText: We use a different register with friends and with a manager.

prompt.es: Elige cómo suena el mensaje de una amiga que perdió el autobús.

choices.text: It sounds warm: she is pleased.
It sounds sarcastic: she is annoyed.
It sounds formal: it is a business email.

feedback.es: Las palabras son positivas, pero la situación (perdió el autobús) muestra enfado: es sarcasmo.

hint.es: Mira qué le pasó a Sara: el autobús se fue.

origin.text: Sara misses the bus and says: “Wow, great timing.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Le agradecería mucho que pudiera enviar el informe.»

feedback.es: Would be grateful if you could es la fórmula formal para pedir algo; grateful significa agradecido.

origin.text: I would be ___ if you could send the report.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Usamos un registro formal con la directora.»

answer.text: We use a formal register with the director

Send it now.

He wants you to turn your music down.
He is asking you to play more music.

A warm thank-you to a colleague.
A formal request to a client.

Fine. The plants are alive.
Wow, great job. You only forgot two of them.

choices.text: A formal letter to a client.
An informal request to a friend.
A sarcastic complaint to a colleague.

es: Repasar en un mismo ejercicio los tags, la deducción (must/can't have), wish, las oraciones enfáticas y la cautela, y corregir frases con errores de cada forma.

vocabulary.es: se podría sostener (it could be argued)

teaching.en: You forgot the tickets again, didn't you?
teaching.es: Olvidaste otra vez las entradas, ¿verdad?
teaching.explanationEs: Tag: el verbo auxiliar cambia de polaridad (forgot → didn't you) y aquí reprocha, no pregunta.
teaching.audioText: You forgot the tickets again, didn't you?

teaching.en: He must have missed the bus; he is never late.
teaching.es: Debe de haber perdido el autobús; nunca llega tarde.
teaching.explanationEs: must have + participio: deducción casi segura sobre el pasado. Lo contrario es can't have.
teaching.audioText: He must have missed the bus; he is never late.

teaching.en: I wish I had more time for my holiday.
teaching.es: Ojalá tuviera más tiempo para mis vacaciones.
teaching.explanationEs: wish + pasado simple: deseo sobre una situación presente que no es así.
teaching.audioText: I wish I had more time for my holiday.

teaching.en: I wish I had listened to my sister.
teaching.es: Ojalá hubiera escuchado a mi hermana.
teaching.explanationEs: wish + had + participio: lamento por algo que pasó. Con would se expresa una queja: I wish you would stop.
teaching.audioText: I wish I had listened to my sister.

teaching.en: It was Tom who broke the window, not Leo.
teaching.es: Fue Tom quien rompió la ventana, no Leo.
teaching.explanationEs: It was + persona + who/that: oración enfática que destaca quién hizo la acción.
teaching.audioText: It was Tom who broke the window, not Leo.

teaching.en: The findings may indicate that sleep helps memory, but it could be argued that more evidence is needed.
teaching.es: Los resultados pueden indicar que dormir ayuda a la memoria, pero se podría sostener que hacen falta más pruebas.
teaching.explanationEs: Cautela académica: may indicate y it could be argued that suavizan la afirmación.
segments: The findings may indicate that sleep helps memory, but
it could be argued that more evidence is needed.
teaching.audioText: The findings may indicate that sleep helps memory, but it could be argued that more evidence is needed.

She must have left early.

hint.es: Después de must have, el verbo va en participio.

feedback.es: Wish + pasado simple (had) expresa un deseo sobre el presente que no es real.

title.es: Analizar la letra de una canción original

es: Analizar el tema, el tono y dos recursos figurados (símil, metáfora, personificación) en la letra de una canción original, leída y escuchada.

teaching.en: This lyric is about the bus ride home at night.
teaching.es: Esta letra trata del viaje a casa en autobús por la noche.
teaching.explanationEs: Lyric es el texto de una canción; empieza el análisis diciendo de qué trata.
teaching.audioText: This lyric is about the bus ride home at night.

teaching.en: The theme is comfort: the singer wants to feel safe at home.
teaching.es: El tema es el consuelo: la cantante quiere sentirse segura en casa.
teaching.explanationEs: El tema es la idea central; el tono (calm, tender) es la actitud o el ambiente.
segments: The theme is comfort: the singer
wants to feel safe at home.
teaching.audioText: The theme is comfort: the singer wants to feel safe at home.

teaching.en: Each verse adds a detail, and the chorus repeats “take me home”.
teaching.es: Cada estrofa añade un detalle y el estribillo repite «llévame a casa».
teaching.explanationEs: La repetición del estribillo subraya la idea principal.
segments: Each verse adds a detail, and
teaching.audioText: Each verse adds a detail, and the chorus repeats “take me home”.

teaching.en: “The city is a sleeping giant” is a metaphor.
teaching.es: «La ciudad es un gigante dormido» es una metáfora.
teaching.explanationEs: Metáfora: dice que A es B, sin like ni as.
teaching.audioText: “The city is a sleeping giant” is a metaphor.

teaching.en: “Like a paper boat on a slow, warm river” is a simile.
teaching.es: «Como un barquito de papel en un río lento y cálido» es un símil.
teaching.explanationEs: Símil: compara dos cosas con like o as.
segments: slow, warm river” is a simile.
teaching.audioText: “Like a paper boat on a slow, warm river” is a simile.

teaching.en: The streetlamps whisper, so the lyric uses personification.
teaching.es: Las farolas susurran, así que la letra usa personificación.
teaching.explanationEs: Personificación: un objeto hace algo que solo hacen las personas.
teaching.audioText: The streetlamps whisper, so the lyric uses personification.

prompt.es: Lee la letra y elige cuál es su tema.

choices.text: Coming home safely after a long day.
Losing a friend in a big city.
Winning a race against the bus.

feedback.es: El estribillo repite «take me home» y el resto describe la ciudad de noche: el tema es volver a casa con calma.

hint.es: Fíjate en el estribillo: Take me home.

origin.text: The city is a sleeping giant tonight, / and I am a small light moving through its dreams. / The streetlamps whisper, “Go slow, go slow.” / Take me home, take me home, / like a paper boat on a slow, warm river.

prompt.es: Elige qué recurso es «The streetlamps whisper».

choices.text: Simile: it uses like or as.
Personification: lamps act like people.
Metaphor: it says lamps are people.

feedback.es: Las farolas no pueden susurrar: darles una acción humana es personificación.

hint.es: Las farolas hacen algo que solo hacen las personas.

prompt.es: Completa: «El estribillo repite la idea principal de la canción.»

feedback.es: El chorus es la parte que se repite entre las estrofas y subraya la idea principal.

hint.es: Es la parte que vuelve entre una estrofa y otra.

origin.text: The ___ repeats the main idea of the song.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada verso con el recurso figurado que usa.

pairs: The moon is a silver plate.

feedback.es: Sin like ni as, «is» da una metáfora; con like o as es un símil; y si el viento canta, hay personificación.

pairs: The moon is a silver plate.

Planning a holiday by the sea.
Winning a school prize.

choices.text: Simile: it uses like to compare.

es: Escribir un relato breve con narrador en primera persona, tiempos narrativos variados (pasado simple, continuo y perfecto), un símil y una oración enfática.

teaching.en: The narrator tells the story and describes the scene.
teaching.es: El narrador cuenta la historia y describe la escena.
teaching.explanationEs: El narrador suele usar el pasado; eligiendo bien el tiempo se ve qué es escenario y qué es acción.
teaching.audioText: The narrator tells the story and describes the scene.

teaching.en: It was raining when I reached the station.
teaching.es: Llovía cuando llegué a la estación.
teaching.explanationEs: Past continuous (was raining) para el escenario; past simple (reached) para la acción puntual.
teaching.audioText: It was raining when I reached the station.

teaching.en: When I arrived, the last train had already left.
teaching.es: Cuando llegué, el último tren ya había salido.
teaching.explanationEs: Past perfect (had left): algo que pasó antes de otro momento del pasado.
teaching.audioText: When I arrived, the last train had already left.

teaching.en: The silence between us was like a wall.
teaching.es: El silencio entre nosotros era como un muro.
teaching.explanationEs: Un símil con like da una imagen: el silencio se compara con un muro.
teaching.audioText: The silence between us was like a wall.

teaching.en: What I remember most is the smell of rain.
teaching.es: Lo que más recuerdo es el olor de la lluvia.
teaching.explanationEs: What + oración + is: énfasis en lo que quieres destacar.
teaching.audioText: What I remember most is the smell of rain.

teaching.en: It was the old key that opened the door.
teaching.es: Fue la vieja llave la que abrió la puerta.
teaching.explanationEs: It was + cosa + that/who: énfasis en quién o qué hizo la acción.
teaching.audioText: It was the old key that opened the door.

prompt.es: Completa: «Llovía cuando salí de casa.»

feedback.es: El escenario del pasado usa was/were + -ing: It was raining.

hint.es: El escenario del pasado usa was/were + -ing.

origin.text: It ___ raining when I left home.

prompt.es: Elige la frase correcta sobre algo que ocurrió antes.

choices.text: When Mia arrived, the film already began.
When Mia arrived, the film had already begun.
When Mia arrived, the film was already beginning.

feedback.es: Had + participio (had already begun) marca que la película empezó antes de la llegada de Mia.

hint.es: Lo anterior a otro momento del pasado usa had + participio.

origin.text: Mia arrived at eight. The film began at seven.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La casa olía como un viejo libro.»

answer.text: The house smelled like an old book

feedback.es: Smelled like + nombre forma un símil olfativo: la casa se compara con un libro viejo.

hint.es: Usa like para comparar la casa con un libro.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del relato con su función.

feedback.es: Was getting dark pinta el escenario, opened es la acción, had lost es lo anterior y like a bright light es un símil.

pairs: It was getting dark.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que enfatiza lo que más recuerda el narrador.

I remember most what is the smell of the bakery.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué ocurrió primero.

choices.text: He made tea before his sister went to bed.
He sat in the kitchen before he reached the house.
His sister went to bed before he arrived.

feedback.es: Had already gone to bed indica que la hermana se acostó antes de que Leo llegara.

origin.audio: When Leo reached the house, his sister had already gone to bed, so he made some tea and sat in the kitchen.

prompt.es: Completa: «Fue mi abuela quien encontró la llave.»

feedback.es: It was + persona + who destaca quién encontró la llave.

origin.text: It was my grandmother ___ found the key.

prompt.es: Escribe el relato: dos tiempos narrativos, un símil y una oración enfática.

answer.text: It was raining when I reached the station, and my bag was heavy. I had promised Sara that I would be there at eight, but the last train had already left. The station was almost empty. A man was sleeping on a bench, and a small clock was above the ticket office. I felt cold and afraid. What I remember most is the silence, which was like a wall between me and the rest of the city. I took out my phone, but my phone had no power. Then I heard a voice behind me. It was my old teacher who was standing there with an umbrella! She had seen me from the bus and had followed me inside. She laughed, gave me her phone and said, “Call Sara. She has probably been waiting for you.” I called, and Sara answered at once. She was not angry. In fact, she had missed the train too, and she was waiting at the next station. My teacher bought us all a hot drink while we waited for the next train. We talked about the long day, about our families and about the rain. We met Sara an hour later, and we laughed about the whole night. I will never forget how kind both of them were.
accepted: It was raining when I reached the station, and my bag was heavy. I had promised Sara that I would be there at eight, but the last train had already left. The station was almost empty. A man was sleeping on a bench, and a small clock was above the ticket office. I felt cold and afraid. What I remember most is the silence, which was like a wall between me and the rest of the city. I took out my phone, but my phone had no power. Then I heard a voice behind me. It was my old teacher who was standing there with an umbrella! She had seen me from the bus and had followed me inside. She laughed, gave me her phone and said, “Call Sara. She has probably been waiting for you.” I called, and Sara answered at once. She was not angry. In fact, she had missed the train too, and she was waiting at the next station. My teacher bought us all a hot drink while we waited for the next train. We talked about the long day, about our families and about the rain. We met Sara an hour later, and we laughed about the whole night. I will never forget how kind both of them were.

It was getting dark when I arrived at the cinema, and a long line was waiting outside. I had bought the tickets two days before, but when I looked in my bag, I understood that I had left them at home. My heart was beating like a drum. What I felt most was shame, because Leo had already told everyone that the film was his idea. I walked to the desk and explained the problem. The woman smiled and said, “Do not worry. Show me the message on your phone.” I looked for it, but my hands were shaking. Finally I found it. It was a small miracle that the message was still there! She checked the name, printed two new tickets and wished us a good film. When I found Leo, the film had already started, so we sat in the dark and whispered like children. Afterwards we walked home and he laughed at me all the way. I remember that night as the day I learned to check my bag twice, and I also remember the woman at the desk, who was kinder than I deserved.

answer.text: Thank you, everyone. I would like to propose a street market on the first Sunday of each month, with stalls for local food and plants. It would bring neighbours together and help small businesses. Tom, I take your point: admittedly, a market may be noisy, and we do not have much money. However, I see it a little differently. With respect, I think the noise would last only a few hours, and the stall fees could pay for the cleaning. I'm afraid I cannot agree that the risk is so big. Could we agree to try it for one month and then review the noise and the cost together? If it does not work, we will stop. Shall we say that we start in October and meet again in November?
accepted: Thank you, everyone. I would like to propose a street market on the first Sunday of each month, with stalls for local food and plants. It would bring neighbours together and help small businesses. Tom, I take your point: admittedly, a market may be noisy, and we do not have much money. However, I see it a little differently. With respect, I think the noise would last only a few hours, and the stall fees could pay for the cleaning. I'm afraid I cannot agree that the risk is so big. Could we agree to try it for one month and then review the noise and the cost together? If it does not work, we will stop. Shall we say that we start in October and meet again in November?

Good evening. I'd like to suggest closing our street to cars on one Sunday a month for a small market. It is true that it could be loud, Tom, and I understand your worry about the budget. Still, I am not sure that the problem is as big as it seems. The stalls would pay a small fee, and volunteers could help clean the street afterwards. What if we agree to a one-month test? Perhaps we could meet again afterwards and decide together whether the market should continue. I believe this is fair for everyone, and I hope you agree.
